To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) the nonverbal behavior of vloggers is significantly correlated with the attention that they receive from the audience, and (2) the most significant nonverbal cues for social attention are the gaze, the facial expressions, the head movements, and the gestures.

(1) vloggers who smile more, speak faster, and have a higher voice pitch tend to attract higher social attention, and (2) vloggers with higher social attention are more likely to be male, have a higher pitch and speak faster.

(1) vloggers who smile and look into the camera are perceived as more friendly and trustworthy, (2) vloggers whose videos are more visually interesting are perceived as more competent, (3) vloggers with higher social attention have a more diverse nonverbal behavior.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of novel multimodal methods for the automatic analysis of vloggers’ conversational behavior and social media attention.
the automatic understanding of conversational behavior in social video, with applications to social media analytics.
the automatic characterization of the social behavior of vloggers and their audience in social media.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
vloggers' nonverbal cues, especially gaze and head movements, are correlated with the social success of vlogs.

the more a vlogger looks at the camera, and the more a vlog is perceived as a "conversation" (i.e., the more the vlogger looks at his/her interlocutors, and the more he/she is perceived as "engaging" and "friendly"), the more social attention a video receives.
the more the vloggers smile and nod, the more social attention they receive, while the opposite happens when they frown and blink.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the automatic analysis of vloggers’ audiovisual nonverball behavior is an effective way to predict the social success of vlogs.
we introduce the automatic analysis and characterization of conversational vlogging, and we present a large-scale study on the social behavior of vloggers.
the more a vlogger smiles, laughs, and looks into the camera, the more attention the video receives.
The main takeaway from our work is that
social attention can be predicted from the analysis of vloggers’ conversational nonverbal behavior.
nonverbal behavior in social media is a new and important research direction in social media understanding.
nonverbal communication in vlogs is an important aspect of the social attention they receive.
